title: Use YNX for the first time
description: Install a wallet, set up a Testnet account and learn to verify an action before trying another.

title: Install YNX Wallet
description: Open the installation guide and choose your actual system or browser. Read the package version and signing status before installing; open the wallet after installation.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Create or restore your own wallet
description: Inside YNX Wallet, choose its own create, import or unlock flow. Record recovery material offline. Use a separate Testnet account while learning.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Add the public Testnet
description: In the wallet's network settings, add or select YNX Testnet using the fields below. Check the network and account before connecting an application.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Request test YNXT
description: Open the official Faucet, enter your Testnet address and follow the current service instructions. YNXT is a test asset with no monetary value.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Inspect a transaction
description: Open Explorer and search your address or transaction hash. Check network, recipient, amount and the displayed result. Before any later transfer, review the wallet's exact confirmation.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Connect and disconnect an application
description: Choose an application, inspect the requested account and permissions, and approve only what you intend. After trying it, disconnect in the app and review connected sites in the wallet.
keywords: Use YNX for the first time

title: Run a learning node
description: Start an isolated Devnet on your computer. Its blocks belong to network 6425 and do not join the public Testnet.

title: Prepare the tools
description: Install Git and Go 1.25 or later. On Windows, use a Linux environment such as WSL for this node tutorial. Open a terminal and check both tool versions.

title: Get a clean source checkout
description: Use a new folder for learning. Clone the repository and select the source version below; keep your existing projects and wallet data separate.

title: Start the local node
description: Run the command from the project root and leave the terminal open. It binds only to your computer and stores learning data in .local/learning-node.

title: Watch blocks grow
description: Open a second terminal and read the local status. Wait several seconds and repeat the same request. Compare network, chainId and height.

title: Stop and resume safely
description: In the node terminal, press Ctrl+C and wait for it to exit. Keep the learning data directory. Run the same start command again to resume.

title: Understand public block production
description: Learn what is available today and what a local experiment does not grant.

title: Know the node roles
description: A producer writes authoritative blocks. Authenticated followers copy state and serve reads. A local learning node produces its own Devnet blocks.

title: Check the current access path
description: Public validator self-enrollment, staking admission and block rewards are not open. An operator must provide the actual configuration, access requirements and authenticated follower connection before public joining is possible.

title: Inspect the local consensus lab
description: In a source checkout, this dry-run shows the local consensus test entry. The actual lab creates temporary teaching keys; it is separate from the public network.

title: Build your first integration
description: Read real network data, then add one capability at a time with explicit wallet approval.

title: Choose a workspace
description: Open Code or use your own editor and a fresh repository checkout. Choose your language, create a small file, run it and read the output. In Code, use the server's default AI or configure your own provider in its settings.

title: Read the network ID
description: Run this public read-only request in a terminal. It asks for network identity and requires no wallet, account or private key.

title: Use the SDK from the checkout
description: With Node.js 18 or later, run this command from the repository root. It imports the local JavaScript SDK and checks a public Testnet snapshot. Python 3.9 or later is also supported by the source SDK.

title: Add an explicit wallet interaction
description: Build account connection as a user action. Show the selected provider, network and requested scope. Ask separately before signing or sending, then inspect the returned outcome.

title: Test before sharing
description: Run the repository's SDK checks in its documented environment. Test timeouts, wrong network, unavailable data and rejected wallet requests. Compile contracts locally only within currently supported tooling.

title: Export, review and publish deliberately
description: Export or package the project, inspect the files for secrets, and test its full-stack preview. Review the intended host, environment variables and permissions before a separate publishing action.
